# Appendix: Git in 10 Minutes for RStudio Users {#sec-git-appendix}

You already know the shell — Git is the natural next step for version-controlling R projects. Everything below also maps to RStudio's Git pane (Tools -> Version Control).

## Configure once

```{bash}
#| eval: false
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
```

## The 6-command workflow

| Step | Shell | RStudio Git pane |
|:-----|:------|:-----------------|
| 1. Check state | `git status` | Diff / status list |
| 2. Stage | `git add file.R` (or `git add -u`) | Tick the Staged box |
| 3. Commit | `git commit -m "feat: short message"` | Commit button |
| 4. Sync down | `git pull` | Pull button (blue down arrow) |
| 5. Sync up | `git push` | Push button (green up arrow) |
| 6. History | `git log --oneline -10` | History button |

## Branches

```{bash}
#| eval: false
git branch feature          # create
git switch feature          # move to it
git switch -c hotfix        # create + move in one step
git switch master           # back to production branch
```

Rule of thumb from this book's workflow: do work on a feature branch, keep `master` deployable, and push only at the end of a phase.

## Ignore files

Create a `.gitignore` so generated files never get committed:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
cat .gitignore
```

```text
.Rhistory
.RData
cline/
docs/
```

This book's own `.gitignore` keeps the `cline/` working directory and rendered `docs/` output out of version control — the same pattern works for your R projects (`data/`, `output/`, `.Rhistory`).

## Undo safely

- Wrong stage: `git restore --staged file.R`
- Wrong edit (file still uncommitted): `git restore file.R`
- Never rewrite history on shared branches — prefer a new commit that fixes the mistake.

## Exercises

1. In a scratch folder, run `git init`, create `notes.R`, then `git status`, `git add notes.R`, `git commit -m "docs: first notes"`, and `git log --oneline`. You should see exactly one commit.
2. Edit `notes.R`, run `git status` (file shows as modified), stage and commit again. `git log --oneline` should now show two commits.
3. Add a `.gitignore` containing `*.html`, create `report.html`, and run `git status` — the HTML file should not appear. Remove it with `rm report.html`.

Worked solutions in `solutions/git-appendix.md` (attempt first).
